test_title: PYST 25: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 20 Aug, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Under Article 244(2) of the Constitution of India, the provisions of the Sixth Schedule apply to the administration of tribal areas in which of the following sets of States?

options.text: Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and Chhattisgarh
Nagaland, Manipur, Meghalaya and Arunachal Pradesh
Bihar, Odisha, West Bengal and Assam

solution:
The correct answer is __**Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Under **Article 244(2)** of the **Constitution of India**, the **Sixth Schedule** applies to the administration of tribal areas in the **northeastern states** of **Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram**.
 
• The **Sixth Schedule** provides for the formation of **Autonomous District Councils (ADCs)** to govern tribal areas, ensuring their customs, governance, and land rights are protected.
 
• Each Autonomous District Council has legislative, administrative, and judicial powers over subjects such as land management, forest resources, village administration, and more.
 
• The provision emphasizes **self-governance** for distinct tribal communities to preserve their cultural and social practices.
 
• Other states listed in the options like Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Chhattisgarh, Nagaland, Manipur, and Arunachal Pradesh are not covered under the **Sixth Schedule**. *Hence, only the states listed in Option 2 are correct.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sixth Schedule of the Indian Constitution:**

 
 
• Introduced to protect the rights and autonomy of **tribal communities** in the northeastern region of India.
 
• Provides for the establishment of **Autonomous District Councils (ADCs)** in tribal-majority areas, allowing them to govern independently.
 
• Each ADC has legislative, judicial, and financial powers, including the ability to collect taxes and manage resources.
 
• ADCs can make laws on land use, forest management, agriculture, water resources, and inheritance, among other subjects.
 
 
 
• **States Covered Under the Sixth Schedule:**
 
 
• **Assam:** Includes tribal areas such as Karbi Anglong, Dima Hasao, and the Bodoland Territorial Region (BTR).
 
• **Meghalaya:** Includes Khasi Hills, Garo Hills, and Jaintia Hills.
 
• **Tripura:** Includes the Tripura Tribal Areas Autonomous District Council.
 
• **Mizoram:** Includes Chakma, Lai, and Mara Autonomous District Councils.
 
 
 
• **Difference Between Fifth and Sixth Schedule:**
 
 
• The **Fifth Schedule** deals with the administration of **tribal areas** in states other than those in the northeast (e.g., Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Odisha).
 
• The **Sixth Schedule** is specifically for the administration of tribal areas in the northeastern states (Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram).
 
• While the Fifth Schedule provides for a **Tribes Advisory Council**, the Sixth Schedule establishes **Autonomous District Councils** with significant legislative and administrative powers.
 
 
 
• **Autonomous District Councils (ADCs):**
 
 
• Each ADC comprises members elected by the people and some nominated by the Governor.
 
• ADCs have the authority to enact laws on land, forest management, and customary laws.
 
• They also have judicial powers to establish village courts for resolving disputes.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical Background:**

 
 
• The Sixth Schedule was included in the Constitution based on the recommendations of the **Bordoloi Committee**, which was set up by the Constituent Assembly to address tribal issues in the northeast.
 
• The primary aim was to balance **tribal autonomy** with national unity.
 
 
 
• **Governor's Role:**
 
 
• The **Governor** of the state has special responsibilities under the Sixth Schedule, such as modifying the jurisdiction of ADCs and approving certain laws enacted by them.
 
• The Governor can also dissolve or reconstitute an ADC if necessary.
 
 
 
• **Significance:**
 
 
• The Sixth Schedule ensures that tribal communities can preserve their **distinct identity, culture, and traditions**.
 
• It provides a mechanism for **self-governance** and development while safeguarding land and resource rights.
